BiblicalUsage: To plow is the work of the servant in the field, and it is used twice. Jesus asks which of you, having a servant plowing, would say to him, sit down to meat, and Paul says he that ploweth should plow in hope, and he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for plowing carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that the work of the field is done in hope, and the labourer who plows in hope has a share in what grows.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
